text:
Maya S. (Support): FYI received an escalation from Darren at Acme. He says post-rollout the chatbot is returning wrong policy text for refund questions. says it's 'outdated' language. attaching convo snippets.
Darren L. (customer): @Maya It's high priority. We pushed v2026-02-12 to prod last night. Before that the bot cited the company refund policy correctly; now it gives a generic 'contact support' reply. This broke several replies in the wild.
Maya S. (Support): Thanks. Did you capture message IDs/times? any reproducible prompt?
Darren L. (customer): Yep. Example prompt: "What is the refund policy for delayed shipments?" cURL to our API:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' \
  -d '{"model":"acme-qa-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the refund policy for delayed shipments?"}], "cache_prefix": "user-123"}'
```
Response we get (short): "Please contact support for refund info." Should have been the paragraph starting with "Refunds are issued..."
Maya S. (Support): Reproduced quickly in our sandbox with same model id and no special headers — got the short response. Opening escalation to SRE/ML.
Owen R. (SRE): Looking at infra logs for that rollout window. Deploy bot shows canary passed, but there was a backend restart at 02:14 UTC on that host pool. grabbing logs now.
deploy-bot: canary deploy v2026-02-12 -> prod: 6/6 instances healthy.
Owen R. (SRE): Stack: runtime v3.4.1, kv-cache service v1.8. noticed many cache hits after rollout for prefixes related to acme-qa-v1. seeing a spike in TTL evictions + stale-hit counters.
Priya K. (Eng-ML): Key suspicion: prefix/KV cache is not namespaced by model variant/rollout id. If the new model variant changes system prompt or tokenization behavior, cached KV prefix entries from previous model may be reused and lead to mismatched continuations.
Owen R. (SRE): Here's a sample of the cache key pattern we saw: `prefix:<customer_id>:model:acme-qa-v1:prefetch:<prefix_hash>` No rollout tag. So new rollout could reuse the same key.
Maya S. (Support): So we'd get short/generic outputs because the KV cache contains old key-value pairs optimized for the previous model weights?
Priya K. (Eng-ML): Exactly. The cached KV/activation state is model-specific. Reusing it can bias generation. Fix options: 1) Invalidate (flush) prefix cache on rollout, 2) Add model_version/rollout_id into cache namespace, 3) Add compatibility/version tag into cache entries and reject mismatched ones.
Owen R. (SRE): For immediate mitigation we can invalidate per-customer prefix entries for acme-qa-v1. Running a targeted flush: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "prefix:acme-*:model:acme-qa-v1:*" | xargs redis-cli del` Planning window in 10 mins, notifying customer.
Darren L. (customer): Please do that ASAP. We're getting complaints.
Maya S. (Support): Scheduling the flush now and will monitor. I'll also offer Acme a rollback option if issues persist.
(deploy-bot) Notice: maintenance window starting for targeted key flush.
Owen R. (SRE): Flushed keys at 02:45 UTC. After flush, I repro'd the prompt — got the expected long refund paragraph. Looks like flush fixed it for requests hitting freshly warmed state.
Darren L. (customer): Confirmed on our side. Thanks — replies look correct now. Any risk of repeated reoccurrence on next rollout?
Priya K. (Eng-ML): Yes risk remains if we don't change cache semantics. I'll open PR to include `model_commit_hash` + `rollout_id` into cache key composition. Also add a runtime check: when loading a prefix entry, verify stored `model_signature` matches current model; if mismatch, treat as miss and garbage-collect old entry async.
Owen R. (SRE): Work items: 1) immediate: add automated prefix cache invalidation in the rollout pipeline (canary -> full) 2) mid-term: change cache keyning to include model signature 3) add metrics for model-mismatched cache hits. I've created SRE ticket #INF-4321.
Maya S. (Support): PRs/tickets? need ETA to update customer.
Priya K. (Eng-ML): PR opens in ~30m, will pass review by EOD. Expect rollout of change next week (staged). I'll include tests: synthetic regression that simulates two model variants and asserts no cross-variant hits.
Owen R. (SRE): Also adding a temporary alert: if stale-hit ratio > 2% for a model within 1h of rollout, fire pager to infra-oncall.
Darren L. (customer): Appreciate the quick triage. Please send postmortem and action items. Also would like a config option to auto-invalidate per-tenant on new model releases.
Maya S. (Support): Noted. We'll offer auto-invalidate toggle to Acme as a short-term account setting (support-run) while infra change lands.
Priya K. (Eng-ML): Follow-up architecture note I'll add to docs: cache entries should include a minimal `model_signature` blob (model_id, commit_hash, tokenizer_version, system_prompt_hash). That keeps in-proc check cheap.
Owen R. (SRE): Postmortem draft: root cause = KV/prefix caching reused across model rollouts due to missing model namespace. Impact = wrong/mismatched outputs for some customers after v2026-02-12 rollout; mitigation = targeted cache flush + rollback available; fix = cache key changes + rollout invalidation + alerting.
Maya S. (Support): I'll send the customer the summary and link to the PM/engineering tickets. Closing the support thread once we have PR merged and infra rollout scheduled.
Darren L. (customer): Thanks everyone. Nice triage.
Maya S. (Support): tagging follow-ups: #INF-4321 (SRE), #ML-1902 (Eng-ML PR), and customer note queued.
Priya K. (Eng-ML): Adding unit tests + integration test with redis mock to prevent regression. Also will add a small migration: when upgrading runtime, default to invalidating cache unless `preserve_cache=true` explicitly set.
Owen R. (SRE): Logging action: export list of flushed keys for audit and customer transparency.
Maya S. (Support): End of thread — will update thread_ts when postmortem is published.
